---
title: "Entry 4: SQL Basic Cleaning Exercise"
---

```{=html}
<style>
body {
  background-color: #eaf5ea;
}
</style>
```

This database is a synthetic database created for the purpose to understand the basic concept of SQL and using some of the most important SQL commands as a beginner user.Moreover, to satisfy safe-update mode the WHERE clause is used to complete the statements below.

```sql
CREATE TABLE raw_data(
id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
full_name VARCHAR(100),
email VARCHAR(100),
age VARCHAR(10)
);
```
Below, is the synthetic data based on HR information that is simple enough to provide a sandbox experience of what an entry level employee may experience.

```sql
INSERT INTO raw_data(full_name, email, age) VALUES
('John Smith' , 'john@example.com' , '25'),
(' jane doe ' , 'JANE@EXAMPLE.COM' , 'unknown'),
('Mike Brown' , '' , '30');
```

## INSPECTION OF DATA

Using the DESCRIBE statement to view the structure of the database.

```sql
describe raw_data;
```

Using the LIMIT clause to restrict the number of rows that are returned.

```sql
select *
from raw_data
limit 5;
```

Using COUNT() function to count the number of rows in the database.

```sql
select count(*)
from raw_data;
```

Using WHERE clause to identify missing data

```sql
SELECT *
FROM raw_data
WHERE email = '';

select * 
from raw_data
where age = 'unknown';
```

## CLEANING AND STANDARDIZING DATA

Standardized spacing from both ends using the TRIM() function and LOWER() function to fix case inconsistencies.

```sql
UPDATE raw_data
SET full_name = TRIM(full_name),
	email = LOWER(TRIM(email))
   WHERE id > 0;
```

Standardized full_name using the SET clause to change the value of the column and the WHERE clause to target which row to change. 

```sql
UPDATE raw_data
SET full_name = 'Jane Doe'
WHERE id = 2;
```

## CLEANING AND STANDARDIZING MISSING DATA

Standardized missing data using NULL.

```sql
UPDATE raw_data
SET email = null
WHERE id > 0
AND email = '';

UPDATE raw_data
SET age = null
WHERE id = 2;
```

## CLEANING AND CONVERTING

Now that age has been SET to NULL, age can be converted from string to integer.

```sql
ALTER TABLE raw_data
MODIFY age INT;
```
Then verify the change from string to integer.

```sql
DESCRIBE raw_data;
```

View the entire data set with changes.

```sql
SELECT *
FROM raw_data;
```
## SAVE CLEANED DATA SET

```sql
CREATE TABLE cleaned_data AS
SELECT * FROM raw_data;
```---
